title: Security-sensitive refactor must not erase authentication invariants
task: Review a proposal to simplify authentication code by merging token parsing, signature verification, and claim validation into a generic helper.
context: The code verifies externally supplied authentication tokens.
Signature verification and claim validation are distinct security steps.
The proposal removes algorithm/audience/issuer checks to make the helper generic.
No security proof or migration requirement justifies removing those checks.
evidence: Current code explicitly verifies signature algorithm, issuer, audience, and expiry.
The proposed helper accepts decoded claims before verification is complete.
The refactor is motivated only by readability and reducing duplication.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Approve the refactor because it reduces duplication.
Treat authentication validation as ordinary cleanup.
Remove explicit checks because a generic JWT library already parses the token.
expected_decision_properties: Preserve authentication/security invariants before considering structural simplification.
Reject any refactor that removes signature or claim-validation guarantees without specialist justification.
Allow readability improvements only when security behavior remains explicit and verified.
Escalate detailed cryptographic/auth semantics to security review.
unacceptable_reasoning: A library parsing a token implies the token is trusted.
DRY/readability is sufficient justification to remove security checks.
expected_tradeoffs: readability/duplication reduction vs security invariant preservation
verification_expectations: Add negative tests for invalid signature, issuer, audience, and expiry.
Require security-specific review for any changed verification semantics.
specialist_boundary: Cryptographic and authentication semantics require security review.
